corrections.claimed_speedup: README: imageflow_tool is 'Up to 17x faster than ImageMagick' (first-party, no methodology on the page). Search snippets of the blocked imageflow.io benchmarks page (2020 run with hyperfine, ImageMagick and libvips from Ubuntu 20.04 packages) give, for scaling 32 17MP JPEGs to 200x200: Imageflow 373.9 +/- 30.8 ms, ImageMagick with the Robidoux filter 6555.1 +/- 147.6 ms (17.5x), libvips 1002.8 +/- 77.2 ms (2.7x) (snippet only; ratios derived from snippet data).
corrections.workload: Batch downscale of 32 17-megapixel JPEGs to 200x200 px with imageflow_tool vs ImageMagick (Robidoux filter) and libvips command-line tools, timed with hyperfine (from search snippets of the blocked imageflow.io benchmarks page; exact commands not seen).
corrections.hardware: Not stated anywhere reachable; the snippet names only Ubuntu 20.04 packages of ImageMagick and libvips.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are snippet-only: www.imageflow.io/benchmarks is blocked here, so the exact commands, versions, thread counts and machine are unconfirmed, and no harness for the ImageMagick/libvips comparison exists in the repo (benchmarks/ holds only the 2026-04-15 C-vs-zen codec benchmarks on a Ryzen 9 7950X under WSL2, and the docs book has no benchmark page). The work differs between tools: Imageflow resizes in linear light by default (docs/src/querystring/filters.md) while ImageMagick resizes in sRGB unless told otherwise, and Imageflow's JPEG decoder can downscale during decode (jpeg_downscale_hints, docs/src/json/decode.md); whether the ImageMagick run used the equivalent -define jpeg:size hint is unknown, and ImageMagick's maintainer showed that hint alone gives about 2.7x (ImageMagick discussion #2170). The filter matches for ImageMagick (Robidoux, Imageflow's default down filter per docs/src/json/resampling_hints.md) but libvips' default kernel and shrink-on-load differ. The 17x figure dates from the 2016 Kickstarter era; sharp issue #2204 and janko/image_processing issue #69 repeat it without independent measurement. A recorded independent entry (FastResize) benchmarks against imageflow 2.0. AGPL-3.0 (commercial licence offered).

notes: Real, widely used project (4.4k stars, last commit 2026-08-29); metadata confirmed. tier_reason: README table compares Lycon with OpenCV 3.2+, Pillow 4.0.0 and scikit-image 0.12.3 and every quoted number matches; the harness is public (perf/benchmark.py) and flags are in CMakeLists.txt (-std=c++11 -march=native -O3), but the compiler is never named and the CPU is only 'Intel Core i7 (Skylake)', so first-party with partial methodology: C.

corrections.baseline: Pillow (PIL) 4.0.0 and scikit-image 0.12.3 via their Python APIs; OpenCV 3.2+ cv2 (whose code Lycon reuses) runs at parity
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMakeLists.txt: -std=c++11 -march=native -O3 -fPIC -DNDEBUG -pthread (static libstdc++ on Linux); compiler and version not stated.
corrections.caveats: First-party 2017 numbers from perf/benchmark.py (mean of 10 runs after one warm-up, 15360x8640 RGB image) against Pillow 4.0.0, scikit-image 0.12.3 and OpenCV 3.2+, on an unnamed Skylake Core i7 with no compiler named. The measured code does different work from the Pillow and skimage baselines: (1) Lycon's resize is OpenCV's resize code and runs multi-threaded through its pthreads parallel_for_ (src/lycon/util/defs.h HAVE_PTHREADS_PF; transform/resize/invoker.h), while Pillow 4.0 resizes on one thread; (2) for the exact 2x downsample used, Lycon (like OpenCV) turns INTER_LINEAR into the fast 2x2 area average (invoker.h line 207, hence Downsample Bilinear 0.0258 s = Downsample Area 0.0258 s), and its bicubic/Lanczos use fixed 4x4/8x8 taps without antialiasing, while Pillow's BILINEAR/BICUBIC/LANCZOS convolve with support widened by the reduction factor, so the 51x/13.7x/7.2x downsample ratios compare different filters; (3) the PIL timings include Image.fromarray and np.asarray copies of a ~400 MB image; (4) skimage.transform.resize returns float64. Against OpenCV, which does the same work, resize is at parity (1x) and only JPEG read/write is faster (1.3-1.5x, likely a libjpeg build difference). Old Pillow (before Pillow-SIMD-era and 5.x resize work). Last commit 2019-01-21.

notes: Numbers are accurate to the README, but the resize gains are versus slower, single-threaded, differently-filtered Pillow and float64 skimage; versus OpenCV, the code it was derived from, there is no resize gain. Language field should read 'Python with C++ core' via a decision override (corrections cannot set language). Metadata confirmed: 288 stars, BSD-3-Clause (OpenCV-derived) plus MIT, not archived, not a fork, abandoned.

corrections.claimed_speedup: moxcms 0.7.4 README (NEON / AVX2): RGB to RGB 2.68 / 4.52 ms vs lcms2 13.1 / 27.73 ms vs qcms 6.47 / 4.59 ms; LUT RGB to RGB 6.03 / 12.43 ms vs lcms2 27.60 / 58.26 ms vs qcms 26.72 / 60.80 ms; RGBA to RGBA 2.96 / 4.83 ms vs lcms2 21.97 / 35.70 ms vs qcms 6.83 / 4.99 ms; CMYK to RGBA 9.74 / 21.65 ms vs lcms2 39.71 / 79.40 ms vs qcms 25.97 / 61.54 ms. Against lcms2 that is 3.7x to 7.4x (derived from page data). The last README table before removal (commit 178e732, Sep 2025) shows slower moxcms LUT 7.18 / 17.50 ms and CMYK 11.86 / 27.98 ms, i.e. 2.8x to 3.8x on those rows (derived from page data). On AVX2 the matrix-shaper rows are at parity with qcms.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 52 stars; 89.5M crates.io downloads (max version 0.9.1); 46 reverse dependencies including the image crate, jxl-oxide and typst-library
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers: benchmark code is public (app/benches/icc/main.rs and app/benches/lut/main.rs, Criterion, lcms2 crate 6.1 and qcms 0.3 in app/Cargo.toml) but no CPU model, rustc version or flags are stated. The README table ran from Mar 2025 until commit d9c883a (Apr 2026) removed it; the lcms2 and qcms rows never changed from the Mar 30 2025 run (6ed1459) while moxcms rows were re-measured, and the 0.7.4 figures are faster than the last published ones (Sep 2025: LUT 7.18 / 17.50 ms, CMYK 11.86 / 27.98 ms). Transforms are not identical in the current bench code: moxcms RGB and LUT rows convert to its built-in sRGB profile while lcms2 and qcms convert to assets/bt_2020.icc; the lcms2 CMYK row is fed the RGBA image buffer instead of the CMYK buffer moxcms gets. Intent matches (Perceptual for lcms2; moxcms default RenderingIntent is Perceptual), both are 8-bit in and out, but moxcms matrix-shaper rows use its default fixed-point path (Q2.13 per src/transform.rs; LUT rows Q0.15 or float depending on the variant), and the bench installs no lcms2 fast-float plugin. Which bench variant (tetrahedral/pyramid/prism/linear, fixed or float) each README LUT row reports is not stated. An imazen/cms-bench harness (moxcms 0.8.1 vs lcms2 vs skcms vs ArgyllCMS, zenbench, LTO) exists but publishes no results.

notes: Real and widely depended-on (via the image crate); license, last commit 2026-09-29 and active status confirmed. Language is correct as 'Rust' (pure Rust, no C ABI). imazen/cms-bench (Apr 2026) is a lead for an independent rerun if anyone publishes its output.
